Start Bayesian optimization from a generated initial design

Source: R/integrated-workflow.R
magp_bayes_optimize_from_scratch.Rd

Constructs a quantitative-sequence initial design, evaluates a user-supplied objective at every initial run, and continues with sequential MaGP Bayesian optimization.

Usage

magp_bayes_optimize_from_scratch(
  FUN,
  n_initial,
  q,
  model = c("2d", "full"),
  direction = c("minimize", "maximize"),
  n_iter = 10L,
  xi = 0,
  stop_ei = 0,
  stop_patience = 3L,
  seed = NULL,
  design_control = list(),
  fit_control = list(),
  acquisition_control = list(),
  objective_args = list(),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

FUN

Objective function. It is called with one named argument for each input column. It must return one finite numeric value or a list containing a finite numeric Score or Value component.

n_initial

Number of runs in the generated initial design.

q

Number of components. Must be at least three.

model

Sequence mapping used by the surrogate: "2d" or "full".

direction

Whether FUN is being minimized or maximized.

n_iter

Maximum number of sequential evaluations after the initial design has been evaluated.

xi

Nonnegative exploration offset for expected improvement.

stop_ei

Nonnegative absolute expected-improvement threshold.

stop_patience

Positive whole number of consecutive low-EI evaluations required for early stopping.

seed

Optional nonnegative whole-number seed. It controls the initial design, model fitting, sequence sampling, acquisition starts, and any random values generated by FUN, without changing the caller's random-number state.

design_control

Named list of additional arguments for magp_initial_design(), such as sequence_maxit, quantity_maxit, and alignment_maxit. n, q, and seed are managed by this function.

fit_control

Named list of additional arguments for magp2d_fit() or magpfull_fit(). X, y, and seed are managed by this function.

acquisition_control

Named list of additional arguments for magp_next_point(). The fitted model, direction, exploration offset, reference value, and seed are managed by this function.

objective_args

Named list of fixed additional arguments supplied to FUN after the generated input columns.

verbose

Logical; if TRUE, print one line for every initial and sequential objective evaluation.

Value

An object of class magp_bayes_opt. In addition to the components returned by magp_bayes_optimize(), it contains initial_design, initial_response, initial_evaluations, design_control, and started_from_initial_design.

Details

The generated input columns are named quantity_1 through quantity_q and sequence_1 through sequence_q. The same named-argument objective interface is used for the initial and sequential evaluations.

Use magp_bayes_optimize() instead when completed initial experiments and their responses are already available.

Examples

# \donttest{
objective <- function(quantity_1, quantity_2, quantity_3,
                      sequence_1, sequence_2, sequence_3) {
  quantities <- c(quantity_1, quantity_2, quantity_3)
  sequence <- c(sequence_1, sequence_2, sequence_3)
  -sum((quantities - c(0.2, 0.6, 0.8))^2) -
    0.01 * sum((sequence - c(1, 3, 2))^2)
}
result <- magp_bayes_optimize_from_scratch(
  objective,
  n_initial = 6,
  q = 3,
  direction = "maximize",
  n_iter = 1,
  seed = 1,
  design_control = list(
    sequence_maxit = 100,
    quantity_maxit = 100,
    alignment_maxit = 100
  ),
  fit_control = list(maxeval = 100),
  acquisition_control = list(n_starts = 2, maxit = 20)
)
#> initial run 1 value -0.891944 
#> initial run 2 value -0.363056 
#> initial run 3 value -0.0763889

#> initial run 5 value -0.603056

result$best_point
